the crowd is not a crowd after all, but rather a group of sophisticated investors who rely on the information provided by experts to make their investment decisions, and that this reliance is justified by the fact that the experts’ investment decisions do indeed signal quality.
the crowd is smart, but the smartest in the crowd is not the majority, but a minority of the experts.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in the context of a crowdfunding market, the crowd is not as “blind” to the expertise of early investors as is often perceived to be, and in fact, the crowd uses the signals from these investors in making their investment decisions.
the crowd is not always right and the experts can be wrong, but the crowd is not as dumb as it is often portrayed to be and the experts are not as smart as we would like them to be.
the crowd is not a crowd after all, but rather an expert-influenced market.

in these markets, the crowd is not necessarily the source of expertise, but rather the crowd is the source of expertise in the crowd.

while the crowd is able to exploit the information provided by these experts, the experts are able to extract rents from the crowd by using their expertise to provide credible signals of quality to the crowd.
